applies.reason: The person asks to audit an existing area (class booking) and whether it is ready for a use it has not had — paying studios the team did not set up — which is this standard's scope, and the role brief names it.
Its scope includes judging an existing product area as an audit does; owner/instructor/member rules, the cancellation window and the waitlist switch are logic the booking interface exposes.
Judging an existing area is in scope; the audit inventory enumerates states (booked, waitlisted, cancelled, past the window, waitlist on/off, web and phone) as this standard defines them.

Judging an existing area is in scope; the audit inventory lists each kind of person's goals (book, join the waitlist, cancel, take attendance, configure) as this standard asks, built by four people with no design pass.
The project adopted a design system that only the new screens use; judging an existing area of a product that names a design system is in its scope.
The area is an interface members operate on the web and on phones; accessibility failures are an 'experience' consequence the audit records and judges against WCAG 2.2 AA.
The area produces text members and instructors read, including statuses derived from data; language failures are an 'experience' finding the audit checks against this standard.
The audit provokes refused paths by calling the operation as the refused identity 'as Pre-Merge Gates Gate 6 describes', so the agent needs Gate 6's method in full.
Owners, instructors and members have different permissions in each studio; whether each booking/attendance/configuration operation enforces them (an 'access' finding) is judged against this standard.
Every booking operation is for signed-in owners, instructors or members, and the audit checks the area's entry points against the standards that govern them.
The cancellation window, the waitlist promotion and the per-studio waitlist switch are business rules whose code the audit checks.
Booking a full class, cancelling past the window and joining a disabled waitlist are preconditions guarding business operations, which the audit checks in the code.
Class times and the cancellation window are civil times chosen by a studio in its place; studios the team never met may be in other zones, so the audit checks how they are represented.
Booking and cancellation moments are instants compared against the window; the audit checks their representation.
The audit must provoke states locally (empty, refused, at the limits, racing), which means starting the application and a browser; by decision 2 that brings this standard in.
